requirements.quote: Each connection ID has an associated sequence number to assist in detecting when NEW_CONNECTION_ID or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames refer to the same value.
requirements.condition: For each connection ID managed by the endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the connection ID with a sequence number used to correlate references in NEW_CONNECTION_ID and RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-ID state and frame processing can be inspected to verify that each applicable connection ID has an associated sequence number.

requirements.quote: The sequence number of the initial connection ID is 0.
requirements.condition: For the initial connection ID issued by an endpoint in the Source Connection ID field during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign sequence number 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign any sequence number other than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial connection ID's recorded sequence number can be compared with the fixed value 0.

requirements.quote: If the preferred_address transport parameter is sent, the sequence number of the supplied connection ID is 1.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends the preferred_address transport parameter containing a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign sequence number 1 to the supplied connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign the supplied connection ID any sequence number other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport parameter and the associated connection-ID sequence number are directly observable.

requirements.quote: Additional connection IDs are communicated to the peer using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames (Section 19.15).
requirements.condition: When communicating additional connection IDs to the peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Communicate them using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frames can be inspected to determine how additional connection IDs are communicated.

requirements.quote: The sequence number on each newly issued connection ID MUST increase by 1.
requirements.condition: Whenever an endpoint newly issues a sequenced connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its sequence number to exactly one greater than the preceding newly issued connection ID's sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse, decrease, skip, or otherwise increment the sequence number by a value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of issued connection IDs can be checked for exact unit increments.

requirements.quote: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet are not assigned sequence numbers.
requirements.condition: For the connection ID selected by a client for its first Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the connection ID without an assigned sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a sequence number to that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's first Destination Connection ID and its metadata can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet are not assigned sequence numbers.
requirements.condition: For any connection ID provided by a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the connection ID without an assigned sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a sequence number to that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A Retry-provided connection ID and its metadata can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: When an endpoint issues a connection ID, it MUST accept packets that carry this connection ID for the duration of the connection or until its peer invalidates the connection ID via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame (Section 19.16).
requirements.condition: After an endpoint issues a connection ID and before the connection ends or the peer retires that connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept packets carrying the issued connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject packets merely because they carry that issued, non-retired connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet acceptance can be tested before and after receipt of the corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.quote: Connection IDs that are issued and not retired are considered active;
requirements.condition: When a connection ID has been issued and has not been retired.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the connection ID as active.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat the connection ID as inactive solely while it remains issued and unretired.
requirements.why_checkable: The active set can be compared with issuance and retirement state.

requirements.quote: any active connection ID is valid for use with the current connection at any time, in any packet type.
requirements.condition: For an active connection ID on the current connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit its use at any time and in any packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Restrict its validity to particular times or packet types solely on that basis.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet processing can be exercised across packet types and connection phases with an active connection ID.

requirements.quote: This includes the connection ID issued by the server via the preferred_address transport parameter.
requirements.condition: When the server issued a connection ID through the preferred_address transport parameter and that ID is active.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that connection ID as valid for the current connection at any time and in any packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exclude it from the validity rules applied to other active connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The origin of the connection ID and subsequent packet acceptance are observable.

requirements.quote: An endpoint SHOULD ensure that its peer has a sufficient number of available and unused connection IDs.
requirements.condition: While maintaining connection IDs for a peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the peer has a sufficient number of available, unused connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's available unused connection-ID pool can be observed, but the chunk does not define a measurable threshold for “sufficient.”

requirements.quote: Endpoints advertise the number of active connection IDs they are willing to maintain using the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint advertises how many active connection IDs it is willing to maintain.
requirements.required_behavior: Express that number using the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport parameters can be inspected for the advertised limit.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit.
requirements.condition: When providing connection IDs to a peer that has advertised a limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the number of provided connection IDs within the peer's limit, except for the expressly permitted temporary-excess case.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit without simultaneously causing sufficient retirement of excess IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The peer's advertised limit and the number and retirement effects of provided IDs can be counted.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY send connection IDs that temporarily exceed a peer's limit if the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame also requires the retirement of any excess, by including a sufficiently large value in the Retire Prior To field.
requirements.condition: When sending connection IDs would temporarily exceed the peer's active-connection-ID limit.
requirements.required_behavior: In the same NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, set Retire Prior To high enough to require retirement of every excess connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Temporarily exceed the peer's limit without the same frame requiring retirement of all excess IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting count and the Retire Prior To value in the frame can be evaluated together.

requirements.quote: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame and adding and retiring active connection IDs, if the number of active connection IDs exceeds the value advertised in its active_connection_id_limit transport parameter, an endpoint MUST close the connection with an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.
requirements.condition: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, including all additions and retirements, when the active connection-ID count exceeds the endpoint's advertised active_connection_id_limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keep the connection open after detecting the post-processing limit violation.
requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted frame can produce the excess count, after which connection closure and its error type are observable.

requirements.quote: An endpoint SHOULD supply a new connection ID when the peer retires a connection ID.
requirements.condition: When the peer retires a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Supply a new connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Receipt of retirement and subsequent issuance of a replacement connection ID can be observed.

requirements.quote: If an endpoint provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit, it MAY supply a new connection ID when it receives a packet with a previously unused connection ID.
requirements.condition: When the endpoint has provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit and receives a packet using a previously unused connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to supply a new connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The issued-ID count, peer limit, received packet's connection ID, and any subsequent issuance are observable.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection to avoid the risk of running out of connection IDs;
requirements.condition: For each connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to impose a limit on the total number of connection IDs it issues.
requirements.why_checkable: Issuance behavior can be tested against the endpoint's configured or implemented per-connection cap.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY also limit the issuance of connection IDs to reduce the amount of per-path state it maintains, such as path validation status, as its peer might interact with it over as many paths as there are issued connection IDs.
requirements.condition: When controlling connection-ID issuance and associated per-path state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to limit connection-ID issuance.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's issuance policy and resulting issued-ID count can be observed.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs SHOULD ensure that the pool of connection IDs available to its peer allows the peer to use a new connection ID on migration, as the peer will be unable to respond if the pool is exhausted.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the peer's available connection-ID pool contains a connection ID it can newly use for the migration.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Initiate such migration with no available new connection ID for the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: The peer's available pool at migration initiation can be checked for at least one usable new connection ID.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that selects a zero-length connection ID during the handshake cannot issue a new connection ID.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint selected a zero-length connection ID during the handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake selection and later connection-ID issuance are directly observable.

requirements.quote: A zero-length Destination Connection ID field is used in all packets sent toward such an endpoint over any network path.
requirements.condition: For every packet sent toward an endpoint that selected a zero-length connection ID during the handshake, regardless of network path.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a zero-length Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: Destination Connection ID field lengths can be inspected across all packets and paths directed to the endpoint.
